idea.name: Ad-funded free specials boards in restaurants
idea.one_liner: Give busy restaurants and coffee shops a free dry-erase specials sandwich board, then sell 6 ad slots on it to local service businesses at $600/year each. The board also brings in leads for an agency upsell.
idea.customer: Local service businesses (tax, insurance, realtors, law, painters, HVAC) as advertisers; restaurants and coffee shops as free host locations
idea.offer: 12 months of ad placement on a specials board shown to the host venue's customers (about 7-10k a month), ad design included
idea.revenue_model: One-off upfront annual ad fee per slot ($600, or $900 for two boards). About $3,600 per board per year against about $400 cost.

acquisition_channels.details: Copy-paste Instagram DMs with a photo of the board to restaurant business pages to book an in-person demo (10th-15th DM got the first host)
Visit the venue with the physical board and sign a 12-month hosting agreement. Cold walk-ins went poorly.
Ask the host owner for named referrals (their insurer, attorney, HVAC, regular realtor), then phone those businesses to sell ad slots
Phone the referred businesses (12-20 names per board)
Cold emails and DMs used to fill the first board before referrals
Re-pitch advertisers from previous boards for each new board

ideas.delivery: Founder designs the ads in Canva/ChatGPT image. A local printer prints them onto an aluminium dry-erase sandwich board (about $350), and the founder delivers it with a stand and markers to the host venue. The venue writes its specials on it and keeps it up for a year.

uk_legal_risk.reason: Host acquisition relies on cold Instagram/Facebook DMs to independent restaurants and cafes. Many of these are sole traders or partnerships, and unsolicited marketing DMs to them are banned under PECR. Calling referred tradespeople needs TPS/CTPS screening. Cold email is only allowed to limited companies.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to the referral contact lists. ASA/CAP code applies to the ad content. Some councils require advertising consent for outdoor A-boards on patios or pavements.

ideas.delivery: Rachel handles sales. Her husband builds sites with Claude Code and hosts them on GHL. Reputation management is a GHL snapshot hooked to the client's invoicing that sends review requests by email and SMS and replies to reviews. AI receptionists and chat widgets are deployed through GHL.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Cold email only to limited companies, with an opt-out. Automated review-request texts and emails to clients' customers need a PECR basis (soft opt-in or consent). UK GDPR processor agreements are needed for the client data. CMA/DMCC rules ban fake or incentivised reviews.
